transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what really made me come in is... I just can't shake this feeling lately. Like, at work, I do the buying for this retail chain, mostly electronics and seasonal stuff, and I swear people there, and even some of the vendors we use, they're tracking my buys. Like, specifically watching what I do and messing with the launch numbers just to make me look stupid. Which is crazy because I used to love talking to the vendors. I actually met this one guy from a headphone company last year, and he had this insane collection of vintage walkmans. We talked for like an hour about cassette tapes, which my dad used to collect too. He had this whole basement full of them, mostly classic rock, and he'd always get mad if I touched them... but anyway, yeah, my supervisor keeps showing me these reports trying to prove that nobody's messing with my numbers, but I just know they are. I can feel it.
How long have you been feeling like these people at work are tracking your buys and messing with your numbers?

Um, I'd say roughly ten months now. I know because it started right around the time we were locking in the summer seasonal buys. Which, by the way, the shipping logistics for summer stuff is just a total nightmare now. We had these inflatable pools coming in from overseas, and you can actually track the cargo ships online. Have you ever done that? It's actually crazy, there's this website where you can see every single ship in the ocean, just these little green dots moving so slowly. I spent like three days just watching the dots once when a container was late. My buddy used to work at the port and he said the seagulls down there are massive, like the size of small dogs, and they'll just steal a sandwich right out of your hand if you aren't paying attention... but anyway, yeah, it's been about ten months of knowing they're messing with my numbers. And, um, that's also when the voice started happening, too. So roughly ten months for all of it.
During these past ten months, have there been any periods where your mood felt significantly different, such as feeling extremely low, hopeless, or unusually energetic and elated?

Yeah, actually, there are times where I feel totally different. Like, I'll get these stretches where I feel like the whole city is just opening up for me, you know? Like I'm completely dialed in and I have all this energy. I'll be walking downtown and the architecture just looks so sharp, like the old brick buildings against the glass ones. Have you ever noticed how they mix the zoning downtown? I was reading about city planning the other night, and they used to just build factories right next to houses in the 1800s. There's this one building near my apartment that used to make umbrellas, of all things. I don't know who buys umbrellas anymore, they always break in the wind. My mom bought me one of those fancy windproof ones once, but I left it on the subway. The subway is crazy late at night, by the way... but anyway, yeah, I'll feel amazing, but then if someone at work questions a purchase order or tells me I need to slow down, I just snap. Like, way harder than I mean to. I get so irritable and angry so fast when I'm in that zone.

When you have those stretches where you feel amazing and full of energy, do the feelings that people are tracking your work and the voice you hear continue to happen during those times, or do they only happen when your mood is not elevated?

Oh, no, they definitely keep happening. Even when I'm in that zone. Like, there were a couple weeks where I was barely sleeping at all, just totally wired, and I was talking nonstop to anyone who would listen about these new sneaker trends. Sneaker culture is wild right now, by the way. People are paying like thousands of dollars for shoes they never even wear, they just keep them in these clear plastic boxes like a museum. My cousin tried to start a business cleaning sneakers, bought all these special brushes and foams, but he ended up ruining a guy's vintage Jordans and got sued. He had to sell his car to pay for it, which was a shame because it was this really nice old Honda Civic, the kind you can actually work on yourself without needing a computer to diagnose every little thing... but yeah, anyway, even when I was feeling totally untouchable at work during those weeks, I was still completely convinced the vendors were manipulating my numbers. And the voice was there too, just kind of pushing me, telling me I had to move faster, buy faster. So yeah, the tracking and the voice don't go away just because I feel amazing.

Have there been any periods of at least two weeks where you experienced the voice and the feeling that people are tracking you, but your mood was otherwise stable and not significantly elevated or low?

Yeah, um, there actually was a time like that. Like, I remember this one stretch where things were a lot calmer. I was sleeping more normally, maybe like seven or eight hours a night, and I didn't have that feeling like I was running the whole market or anything. I was just kind of... normal, I guess. But even then, for a few weeks, I still totally believed they were tracking my buys. And I was still hearing the voice when I was back in the stockroom. The stockroom is so dusty, by the way. I don't think they've cleaned the vents back there since the building was built. I was looking up at the ceiling tiles once and you can see this thick layer of gray fuzz just clinging to the metal grates. It makes me wonder what we're breathing in all day, you know? My aunt used to work in a textile mill back in the day and she got this terrible cough from all the cotton fibers in the air. She used to make these amazing quilts, though. Like, really intricate patterns with all these scraps of fabric she'd save. She made me one when I graduated high school that had all these little baseballs stitched into it because I used to play Little League... but anyway, yeah, even when my mood was totally stable and I wasn't super wired, the voice and the tracking stuff were definitely still happening for those few weeks.

Aside from the times you felt amazing and full of energy, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt deeply depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in almost everything, while still hearing the voice or feeling like you were being tracked?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had a time where I felt super down or hopeless for weeks on end like that. I mean, I get tired, sure, especially when the inventory numbers don't match up and I'm just staring at spreadsheets all day. Spreadsheets can really mess with your eyes after a while. I actually had to buy these blue-light blocking glasses online because of it. They were supposed to be next-day delivery, but the shipping got totally messed up because of that huge storm out on the East Coast. Did you see the footage of that on the news? Cars were just literally floating down the street. It’s crazy how fast water can just take over a whole town like that. My buddy lives down in Florida and he says they have to put sandbags by their doors every single hurricane season. He actually uses the leftover sandbags to build a little fort for his dog in the garage. It's a Golden Retriever, they're so goofy, they'll just sleep on anything... but um, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, feeling depressed. Yeah, no, I haven't really felt like that. Just the really high energy times, or just feeling regular.
